question: is there a way to make one specific tool always be the first thing it calls
supported_answer: Set tool_choice to type "tool" and name the tool: the model will use the specified tool with tool_choice.name. Pair it with disable_parallel_tool_use true to get exactly one tool use.

evidence.quote:
- `ToolChoiceTool object { name, type, disable_parallel_tool_use }`

    The model will use the specified tool with `tool_choice.name`.

atomic_claims: tool_choice type tool with a name forces the model to use that specific tool
the tool is named via tool_choice.name
ambiguity_notes: 'Always be the first thing it calls' is the user's framing. The corpus documents forcing a named tool for the turn, not an ordering guarantee across a multi-tool sequence. The answer states the documented mechanism rather than adopting the ordering claim.
verifier_notes: Question said 'either' provider. Anchored in Anthropic because that is where a named-tool choice is documented as a typed object; the OpenAI Agents SDK equivalent (a bare tool-name string) is documented separately and was not needed to answer.

question: streaming + tool calls = arguments come in fragments?
supported_answer: Yes, with fine-grained tool streaming. It delivers a tool's input to your client as Claude generates it, without server-side buffering or JSON validation, so you receive partial fragments rather than one complete validated object.

evidence.quote: Fine-grained tool streaming delivers a tool's input to your client as Claude generates it, without server-side buffering or JSON validation.

atomic_claims: fine-grained tool streaming delivers tool input as it is generated
it skips server-side buffering and JSON validation, so fragments are not validated JSON
critical_strings: without server-side buffering or JSON validation
ambiguity_notes: Question said 'either' provider; answered from Anthropic where the feature is named and documented.
verifier_notes: The 'without JSON validation' clause is the load-bearing part: it is what makes fragments non-parseable mid-stream, which is what the question is really about.

question: enum in schema not being respected
supported_answer: Structured outputs do not guarantee the capitalization of string enum and const values. Claude may return a value differing from the schema only in capitalization, typically in the first letter. Schema compliance is otherwise guaranteed in most cases.

evidence.quote: Structured outputs don't guarantee the capitalization of string `enum` and `const` values: Claude may return a value that differs from your schema only in capitalization

atomic_claims: structured outputs do not guarantee capitalization of enum and const string values
a returned value may differ from the schema only in capitalization
reasoning_type: locating a documented exception to a guarantee
ambiguity_notes: The question does not say how the enum is 'not respected'. The corpus documents exactly one enum-specific failure — casing — so that is what is cited. A different underlying cause would need different evidence.
verifier_notes: Sits in the 'Invalid outputs' section alongside refusal and max_tokens causes; only the enum-casing clause is cited because only it is enum-specific.

question: prefilling assistant turn with { to force json — is that still a thing
supported_answer: No, not on current models. From Claude 4.6 onward, prefilled responses on the last assistant turn are no longer supported and such requests return a 400 error. Earlier models still support prefills, and assistant messages elsewhere in the conversation are unaffected.

evidence.quote: Starting with Claude 4.6 models and [Claude Mythos Preview](https://anthropic.com/glasswing), prefilled responses (providing a partial assistant message for Claude to continue from) on the last assistant turn are no longer supported. Requests with prefilled assistant messages to these models return a 400 error.

atomic_claims: prefilled responses on the last assistant turn are unsupported from Claude 4.6 onward
earlier models continue to support prefills
ambiguity_notes: The '{' prefill trick is the user's specific instance of the general prefill mechanism the corpus deprecates. The answer is version-scoped rather than absolute because the corpus explicitly preserves the behaviour on earlier models.
verifier_notes: Answering a flat 'no' would be wrong: the corpus keeps prefills working on pre-4.6 models. The version scoping is part of the gold answer.
